memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy. Six days you shall labor and do
all your work, but the seventh day is a sabbath to the LORD your God. On it you
shall not do any work, neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your male or
female servant, nor your animals, nor any foreigner residing in your towns.'"
- Ex 20:8-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice who is included in this command: sons, daughters, servants, foreigners,
even animals.

Consider what that meant. Israel had just come from Egypt, where slaves worked
without rest. Now God commands rest for everyone, including the servant and the
outsider. A wealthy Israelite could not rest while making his workers labour. The
command protected exactly the people most likely to be exploited.

Rest, in God's economy, is not a privilege of the powerful. It is a right
extended to the powerless.

Christians differ sincerely on how this applies today, and this is not a
devotional that will settle that. Paul writes that no one should judge others
"with regard to a religious festival, a New Moon celebration or a Sabbath day"
(Col 2:16). Some believers observe a strict day; others see the principle
fulfilled in Christ and applied more freely. Both are held by faithful people.

What is not in question is that we were made to stop. Bodies wear out. Souls dry
up. And a life with no rhythm of rest usually signals that we believe the world
depends on us.

Notice the word "remember." God knew we would forget.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who works so that you can rest, and do they get rest too?
2. What does your inability to stop reveal about what you believe?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that rest is Your gift. Help me to receive it and to make room
for others to receive it too. Amen.
